content:
# Red-team: q\* = m·B_P/B_H split in the verkle-chain provenance gate

**Semantics pinned first.** Path P = proof/witness lane (verkle witness generation + delivery). Path H = header/hash lane (canonical root/header delivery). Total work W is split by ratio q\* = m·B_P/B_H (w_P : w_H), where m is a dimensionless overhead-calibration constant. Honest measurements ⇒ both legs finish at the same instant.

**The invariant that actually matters (call it I):** the gate opens only if, for epoch e, the *single joint commitment*

```
C_e = H("join" ‖ e ‖ q*_fixedpoint ‖ root_P ‖ root_H)
```

matches the expectation pre-committed at epoch start, root_H is canonical and fresh, the provenance depth-D entry verifies, and no nullifier exists for (e, requester). **q\* is not in I.** It is a liveness heuristic. Every serious bypass below either tries to make q\* load-bearing for soundness, or attacks I around it. Mitigations enforce that separation.

---

### A — Poison the measurements (B_P, B_H)

**A1 — Probe precomputation / bandwidth inflation.** Middlebox or peer answers capacity probes instantly with cached responses, inflating B_H (or B_P), skewing q\* to dump work on the wrong leg.
**Fix:** chained-nonce throughput probe: verifier sends chunks carrying fresh nonces n_i; responder returns MAC(n_i ‖ chunk_i) with n_{i+1} = H(n_i ‖ resp_i). Responses cannot be precomputed or parallelized ahead of receipt. Set B := min over j windows. Faking a higher rate requires sustaining it for real.

**A2 — Self-deflation (sandbagging).** Lazy peer reports low B to starve a leg or trip a timeout.
**Fix:** bond-and-slash: peer posts bond against attested B̂; if any window-min < B̂·(1−ε), slash bond and blacklist for the session. Gate uses B̂, never self-reports, until re-earned.

**A3 — Sybil report flooding.** Many fake endpoints flood the measurement aggregator with skewed B values.
**Fix:** stake-weighted median over signed per-pubkey reports; require ≥ 2/3 of bonded stake coverage or fail closed. Sub-majority stake cannot move the median.

**A4 — External congestion on one leg.** Jam P or H at network level to desynchronize finish times.
**Fix:** stop trusting the static split. Greedy chunk scheduler: maintain residuals r_P, r_H; assign each next chunk to argmin(residual); tie → P. q\* is demoted to an initial hint. Any measurement lie costs at most one chunk of misallocation; makespan stays within one chunk of optimal.

---

### B — Poison the formula and arithmetic

**B1 — m tampering via local config.** m sits in a config file/env var; attacker edits it, skewing every split.
**Fix:** m lives at verkle leaf key `cfg/m` under the canonical state root; the gate reads it only via verkle proof against the pinned root. Writes go through governance transactions exclusively.

**B2 — Governance front-running of m updates.**
**Fix:** pin m at the gate's start epoch (m_effective = m_at(start_block)). New values must be published on-chain ≥ E epochs before activation. In-flight gates are immune by construction.

**B3 — Floating-point and degenerate-value exploits.** B_H → 0 (division blowup), truncation driving one leg's allocation to zero, rounding across decision boundaries.
**Fix:** u64 fixed-point throughout (B scaled 2^16, u128 intermediates for m·B_P), defined round-half-up, guards ordered: (1) assert B_P, B_H ≥ B_floor > 0 else abort epoch; (2) n_P = floor(f·N) with largest-remainder distribution of the residue; (3) assert 1 ≤ n_P ≤ N−1. Any breach ⇒ reject. No NaN path exists.

**B4 — Cross-implementation divergence on units.** One client computes q\* over bytes, another over items; honest nodes split differently and partition the gate.
**Fix:** normative definition: q\* over post-serialization byte counts. Committed reference test vectors in-tree; CI enforces bit-exact q\* on all of them. Non-conforming clients are non-canonical.

---

### C — Break the join

**C1 — TOCTOU swap between completions.** P finishes early with valid-looking output; attacker swaps content before H lands; gate sees "both done."
**Fix:** the gate never evaluates two booleans. It performs one atomic comparison of C_e against the pre-committed expectation. There is no state window between "P done" and "H done" because neither fact is recorded individually.

**C2 — Epoch replay.** Replays last epoch's genuinely-concurrent pair to open today's gate.
**Fix:** epoch nonce inside C_e; monotonic gate counter; every consumed (epoch, requester) inserted into a verkle nullifier tree; absence proof required at check time. Replayed commitments fail the nonce match; reused nullifiers fail the absence proof.

**C3 — Fork/header forgery for H.** Present a header from a side fork with a valid-looking quorum certificate; it arrives fast and "completes" H cheaply.
**Fix:** root_H must equal the root pinned by the sync-committee-finalized canonical header, with slot freshness slot_H ≥ head − Δ and quorum ≥ threshold. Anything else is rejected before timing is even considered.

**C4 — Hash-only check / commit-then-diverge.** Announce a root hash early, deliver a divergent body later.
**Fix:** gate compares full-body commitments: body must hash to the announced root *and* the root must pass C3's canonicality check. Both conditions, one conjunction, no exceptions.

**C5 — Timeout-forced fallback.** Congest one leg past timer T so the gate degrades to single-path mode, then attack the weaker single-path check.
**Fix:** the fallback code path does not exist. Timer expiry ⇒ reject and retry under a fresh epoch with fresh nonces. CI carries an assertion that no control-flow edge leads from any timer to an acceptance state.

**C6 — Budget double-claim.** Claim resource credit for one chunk on both paths (relevant if B_P, B_H meter paid throughput).
**Fix:** credit posts only upon inclusion of the chunk-result hash inside C_e; per-chunk nullifier; one claim per chunk id, ever.

---

### D — Game the assignment dynamics

**D1 — Data-dependent clustering.** Contiguous-range splits let an adversary place heavy verkle branches inside one leg's range, so true cost diverges from the byte ratio q\* was computed on.
**Fix:** data-oblivious assignment: chunk i → P iff H("assign" ‖ e ‖ i) mod 2³² < f·2³², where f = m·B_P/(m·B_P + B_H). Deterministic, unbiased, immune to layout crafting.

**D2 — Oscillation attack.** Alternate congestion pulses to keep the estimator in permanent transient, never converging.
**Fix:** deterministic convergence monitor: if |T_P − T_H| / max(T_P,T_H) > δ for 3 consecutive epochs, freeze f at f_safe = B_P,min/(B_P,min + B_H,max) (attested bounds) for L epochs and halve chunk size. At the attested worst-case corner, neither leg exceeds W/(B_P,min + B_H,max). Guaranteed.

**D3 — Chunk-granularity gaming.** Oversized chunks hide skew inside a single allocation.
**Fix:** hard ceiling c_max (fixed 4–64 KiB band, governance-set). Greedy correction (A4) then bounds any residual error by c_max.

---

### E — Verkle/provenance-specific substitutions

**E1 — Wrong-keyset witnesses.** Deliver fast, cryptographically valid witnesses for keys nobody asked about.
**Fix:** for each returned witness, recompute the commitment chain from the claimed (key, value) — stem derivation, extension-node commitment, leaf marker, suffix — and verify the KZG opening against root_P. Additionally, the sorted delivered-key list must hash into the expected root_P; set inequality ⇒ reject.

**E2 — Provenance truncation.** Supply a valid provenance prefix that stops short of required depth; it finishes the race early.
**Fix:** gate pins depth D and anchor A; the ledger stores a running hash at every index, so a single verkle membership proof of key ("prov", D) with value committing to A suffices — O(1), and a truncated chain structurally cannot produce an index-D entry.

**E3 — KZG forgery attempt on the wire.**
**Fix:** full pairing check on (commitment, proof, evaluation) with per-epoch domain separation. No shortcut verification, no batch-skipping on the gate path.

---

### F — Side channels

**F1 — Completion-timing leak.** Microsecond deltas in registration times reveal which provenance branch evaluated true.
**Fix:** buffered constant-time release: gate emits output only at T_release = T_start + ⌈W/B_floor⌉ + δ. Early finishers are held. Timing carries zero information.

---

## Master rules (the actual deterministic core)

1. **Soundness never reads a clock or a bandwidth number.** Invariant I is enforced solely by commitments, signatures, nullifiers, and O(1) verifiable proofs.
2. **q\* may be attacked without limit; the worst outcome is one chunk of misallocation** — a liveness cost, never acceptance of invalid state.
3. **Fail-closed, universally.** Clamp breach, degenerate B, missing attestation, stale slot, nullifier hit, commitment mismatch, timeout ⇒ reject; retry only under a fresh epoch with fresh nonces. No degraded modes exist anywhere in the codebase.

reasoning:
Let me parse this problem carefully. The user is asking about a "measured split q* = m·B_P/B_H" that makes two resource paths finish together, in the context of "verkle chain / provenance gate." They want a red-team analysis: enumerate bypass attempts and deterministic mitigations for each.

This is abstract/obscure terminology — it reads like a constructed or domain-specific problem, possibly from a research paper or a specific system design. Let me try to ground it in what's plausible:

- "Verkle chain" — Verkle trees are a real cryptographic data structure (vector commitments / KZG polynomial commitments over Merkle-style tree structure), used in Ethereum statelessness proposals. A "verkle chain" could be a blockchain using verkle trees for state commitments.
- "Provenance gate" — a gate/checkpoint that verifies provenance (origin/history) of data or resources before allowing passage.
- "Two resource paths finish together" — this sounds like a load-balancing or resource-allocation scenario where two paths (e.g., two execution branches, two data-fetch routes, two compute lanes) must complete simultaneously.
- "q* = m·B_P/B_H" — a measured split ratio. B_P and B_H likely denote bandwidths or budgets of two paths: B_P = bandwidth/capacity of path P (provenance path?), B_H = bandwidth/capacity of path H (header/hash path? history path?). m is some multiplier or margin factor. q* is the fraction/split assigned to one path so both finish at the same time.

Classic problem: if you have two channels with capacities B_P and B_H, and you need to split work so they finish simultaneously, the split ratio should be proportional to capacity: assign fraction q to path P and (1−q) to path H such that q/B_P = (1−q)/B_H → q = B_P/(B_P+B_H). With a multiplier m: q* = m·B_P/B_H... hmm, that doesn't immediately match unless m normalizes.

Actually let me think: if total work W is split as qW to path P and (1−q)W to path H, finish times are qW/B_P and (1−q)W/B_H. Equal when q/B_P = (1−q)/B_H → q·B_H = (1−q)·B_P → q(B_H + B_P) = B_P → q = B_P/(B_P+B_H).

Alternatively, if the split is expressed as a ratio r = (work to P)/(work to H), then r* = B_P/B_H. So q* = m·B_P/B_H where m might be a safety/measurement margin multiplier (e.g., measured vs nominal calibration constant), and q* is the ratio of work assigned to P versus H.

So the system: in a verkle-chain-based provenance gate, there are two resource paths — plausibly:
- Path P: proof/provenance path (fetching/generating proofs, e.g., verkle witness generation)
- Path H: header/hash path (fetching chain headers/hashes)

And the gate opens only when both paths finish; the scheduler splits work by q* = m·B_P/B_H to make them finish together (simultaneity requirement — maybe for atomicity: the gate must open with both pieces arriving at once, preventing partial-state attacks like TOCTOU).

The red-team question: enumerate bypass attempts against this simultaneity/split mechanism and give deterministic mitigations.

The user wants: concrete, exact, grounded, no fluff. So I should:

1. Briefly pin down the mechanism and its security property (what invariant does q* enforce).
2. Enumerate bypass attempts (attack vectors) — each concretely described: what attacker does, which parameter they manipulate, what failure results.
3. For each, give a deterministic mitigation — exact rule/formula, not probabilistic hand-waving.

Let me enumerate attack surface systematically. The formula q* = m·B_P/B_H depends on three inputs: m (margin/calibration), B_P (path P capacity measurement), B_H (path H capacity measurement). The enforcement point is the gate (both must finish together). The environment is a verkle chain (so witnesses, KZG commitments, state roots) and a provenance gate (attestation of origin).

Attack classes:

A. Measurement manipulation (attacker skews B_P or B_H):
1. Bandwidth inflation on one path: attacker floods path H with junk traffic to inflate measured B_H, causing scheduler to over-assign work to H... wait, if B_H appears inflated, q* = m·B_P/B_H decreases, meaning less relative work to P (if q is P:H ratio) — actually let me define carefully. Let me define q* as the share going to path P: share_P = q*/(1+q*) if q* is a ratio, or maybe q* is directly the fraction. To be safe I'll treat q* as the P:H work ratio. If attacker inflates B_H (fake capacity), then q* shrinks → more work pushed to H relative to P → H finishes late → gate stalls (DoS) or, worse, if there's a timeout fallback, the fallback path gets triggered (bypass!). If attacker deflates B_P (congests P), q* shrinks too... wait deflating B_P also shrinks q*. Hmm: inflating B_H shrinks q*, deflating B_P shrinks q*. Both push work toward H. Conversely inflating B_P or deflating B_H raises q*, pushing work toward P.

Key insight: any adversary who can bias the measurements can skew the split, creating either (a) desynchronization — paths finish apart, breaking the simultaneity invariant, enabling TOCTOU at the gate; or (b) starvation/DoS; or (c) forced fallback onto an insecure slow path.

Deterministic mitigations: 
- Use signed/timestamped capacity attestations from the transport layer itself (e.g., QUIC path validation, or explicit probe tokens signed by the gate) rather than passive measurement.
- Clamp: q ∈ [q_min, q_max] hard-coded bounds derived from worst-case verified capacities; anything outside triggers re-probe, not adaptation.
- Two-of-N measurement consensus: measure over k independent intervals, take median, require agreement within tolerance ε else fail-closed.
- Make the split self-correcting: closed-loop with per-chunk acks; recompute residual split each round-trip from actual completion counts, not predicted capacities. Deterministic rule: after each epoch t, set q_{t+1} = clamp(q_t · (T_P,t/T_H,t)^α ... hmm, but they want deterministic mitigations, not control-theory fluff. Better: exact rebalancing rule — assign next chunk to whichever path has larger remaining-time estimate; this converges exactly regardless of initial estimate. That's the classic "greedy list scheduling" which is optimal-ish and removes dependence on accurate B estimates entirely. Actually the strongest deterministic mitigation: don't precompute a static split from measured bandwidths at all; use dynamic work-stealing with unit-sized chunks and a join barrier. Then no measurement can bias the final schedule beyond one chunk granularity. But the problem states the system uses q* = m·B_P/B_H, so mitigations should keep the architecture but harden it.

B. Split-formula manipulation:
2. Parameter m tampering: m is a config/calibration constant. If stored mutable (config file, env var, governance param), attacker sets m large/small to skew everything. Mitigation: commit m into the chain's genesis/state root (it's a verkle chain — put m as a leaf in the verkle tree covered by the state root, updated only via signed governance transaction with delay); gate reads m via verkle proof against the canonical root. Deterministic: m must be verkle-proven, not read from local config.

3. Rounding/truncation exploit: q* computed in floating point; attacker crafts B_P, B_H values so rounding pushes allocation across a boundary (e.g., integer division truncation gives 0 to one path). Mitigation: fixed-point arithmetic with defined rounding mode (round-half-up at 2^-32 granularity), plus assert q* ≥ 1 and q* ≤ Q_max; fail-closed on violation. Exact: compute numerator = m_num · B_P_denom... specify: represent all quantities as u64 fixed-point; q*_num = m·B_P, q*_den = B_H; allocate floor and track remainder deterministically (largest remainder method) so sum of allocations equals total exactly.

C. Gate-level bypasses (the simultaneity/join):
4. TOCTOU at the gate: attacker makes path P finish early with stale-but-valid-looking data, then swaps content between P-completion and H-completion. If the gate checks "both done" without binding contents, the pair presented isn't the pair computed. Mitigation: bind both paths' outputs into a single commitment checked atomically: gate verifies verkle_proof(P_output || H_output) against expected root; i.e., the join condition is not "two booleans" but "one aggregate hash matches." Deterministic: single 32-byte equality check over H(P_out ‖ H_out ‖ epoch ‖ q*_used), committed before execution.

5. Replay/stale-epoch: attacker replays last epoch's completed pair (both genuinely finished together then) to open the gate now without doing work. Mitigation: epoch nonce in the commitment; gate keeps monotonic counter; reject any commitment whose epoch ≠ current; store last-used nonces in verkle tree (nullifier set) to prevent cross-fork replay. Deterministic nullifier check.

6. Partial-completion forgery: attacker claims H finished by presenting a header signature from a minority/forked chain (in a verkle chain context: a header from a side fork with valid-looking quorum). Mitigation: gate accepts H-output only under the canonical root: verify the header's state_root against the verkle root pinned by the light-client committee (sync committee / staking quorum) with a freshness bound (slot ≤ current − k). Deterministic: signature-set size ≥ threshold AND slot freshness AND root match; else reject.

7. Timeout-forced fallback bypass: many systems have "if paths don't finish together within T, proceed with whichever finished" — attackers just congest one path to force fallback onto the single-path mode, then attack single-path mode (which presumably lacks the cross-check). Mitigation: fail-closed — no fallback exists; on timeout the gate rejects and the whole request re-executes under a fresh epoch with penalized parameters (e.g., halve chunk size). Deterministic: timeout ⇒ reject, never degrade.

8. Split-injection via adversarial chunk boundaries: if the split assigns contiguous ranges (P gets first q fraction of the index space, H the rest), attacker manipulates data layout so expensive items cluster in one range (e.g., heavy verkle branches placed in P's range), making true cost ratios diverge wildly from byte ratios. Mitigation: interleave assignment by cryptographic shuffle: chunk i goes to P iff bit_i(H(chunk_id ‖ epoch)) = 1 with probability matched to q* — i.e., hash-based weighted assignment per chunk, so no data-dependent clustering survives. Deterministic PRP-based assignment.

9. Capacity-measurement poisoning via probe spoofing: B_P and B_H are measured with probes; attacker (a middlebox or malicious peer) answers probes instantly (precomputed responses) to inflate apparent bandwidth, or drops them to deflate. Mitigation: probes carry unpredictable nonces requiring computation proportional to claimed bytes (proof-of-throughput: responder must return HMAC(nonce, chunk_i) for i=1..n where chunks are sent only after nonce commitment — can't precompute); take min over windows rather than average (min is monotone and unspoofable upward: you can't fake being faster than your true min under this scheme... well, precomputation is blocked by nonce chaining). Also cap: B_used = min(B_measured, B_attested_by_peer_stake). Deterministic: B := min(measured_min_window, bonded_attestation).

10. Sybil/multi-path confusion: attacker presents many sub-paths aggregating reported bandwidth. Mitigation: identity-bound measurement — each path endpoint signs its measurement report; reports aggregated per distinct pubkey with stake-weighted median; sybils dilute only if stake allows. Deterministic rule: B_path := stake_weighted_median(reports), require ≥ 2/3 stake coverage else fail-closed.

11. Timing-side-channel on the gate check itself: attacker observes microsecond differences in when the two completions register to infer internal state (e.g., which branch of provenance succeeded) — not exactly a bypass of q* but a leak through the simultaneity mechanism. Mitigation: constant-time join: gate releases result only at fixed deadline T_end = start + ceil(W/B_min_verified) regardless of actual finish times; buffer early finisher. Deterministic: release-at-deadline semantics.

12. Manipulating m indirectly via governance capture / update transaction front-running: attacker submits m-update tx and front-runs dependent operations. Mitigation: m updates take effect only at epoch boundaries with a disclosure delay (publish root of new m at least E epochs ahead); all in-flight gates pin m at their start epoch. Deterministic: m_effective(gate) = m_at(gate.start_epoch).

13. Numerical edge cases: B_H = 0 (path down) → division by zero / infinite q*. Attacker induces B_H→0 by jamming, hoping implementation crashes or defaults to all-on-P. Mitigation: explicit guard: if B_H < B_floor or B_P < B_floor ⇒ abort epoch, mark path unhealthy, require N consecutive healthy probes before reuse. Fail-closed, deterministic.

14. Verkle-specific: witness substitution. Path P returns verkle witnesses for keys other than those requested (valid proofs, wrong keys) — finishes fast because it precomputed witnesses for a different key set. Gate must verify key-binding: each witness proves (key, value) pairs whose hashes concatenate into the requested commitment. Deterministic: recompute stem commitment from returned (key,value) and compare to the leaf in the path given by key bits; plus check the extension/status node. This is standard verkle verification — spell it out.

15. Provenance-gate-specific: provenance chain truncation — attacker supplies a valid provenance prefix that terminates earlier than required depth (finishes faster, wins the race, gate sees "provenance complete"). Mitigation: gate pins required depth D and anchor root; verify length via the verkle-encoded provenance ledger: prove that entry at index D exists and equals anchor; shorter chains simply cannot produce the index-D proof. Deterministic membership proof at fixed index.

16. Race the recomputation loop: if mitigation uses adaptive rebalancing, attacker oscillates congestion to keep the estimator in transient forever (never converges, always mis-split). Mitigation: bounded convergence — after k epochs force the conservative static split q_static = clamp with worst-case bounds and enlarge chunk granularity; or switch to work-stealing which needs no estimate. Deterministic: after k=3 failed convergence checks (|T_P − T_H| > δ), freeze q at q_safe = B_P,min/(B_P,min+B_H,max) computed from attested floors/ceilings — guaranteed both paths ≤ W/B_floor time.

17. Commit-then-diverge on H: attacker sends header hash quickly (cheap) matching P's timing, but the full header body arrives later/different — gate keyed on hash-only comparison. Mitigation: gate compares full bodies' commitment, not just root hash; require the header body to hash to the announced root AND the root to be canonical (see #6).

18. Exploiting m's units/semantics ambiguity: if m multiplies B_P/B_H but implementations disagree whether q applies to bytes or items, a cross-implementation consensus split diverges (two honest nodes split differently → different gate epochs → partition). Mitigation: spec-pin: q* defined over byte-counts post-serialization, with a reference test vector set committed in-tree; CI enforces bit-exact q* on vectors. Deterministic conformance suite.

That's a lot. The user asked to "enumerate the bypass attempts and the deterministic mitigation for each. Be concrete, exact, grounded." So format: probably a table or structured list: Attack ID | Vector | Mechanism (what parameter it corrupts, what breaks) | Deterministic mitigation (exact rule).

I should also briefly state the invariant being defended: the gate opens iff both paths' outputs, produced under the same epoch and same q*, jointly hash to the expected commitment — simultaneity is a means to prevent partial-result consumption; q* is a performance heuristic, and the red-team lesson is: never let a performance heuristic carry security weight. The deepest deterministic mitigation: decouple security from q* entirely — q* may be gamed, but gaming it must only cost liveness/performance, never soundness. That's the architectural principle: q* influences scheduling; correctness enforced by commitments independent of timing.

Let me structure the answer:

1. Pin the mechanism (short): definitions, invariant, trust assumptions. Define: two paths P (proof/witness path) and H (header/hash path) in a verkle-chain provenance gate; scheduler splits workload W by ratio q* = m·B_P/B_H so both finish at T ≈ same time; gate joins them. Invariant I: gate output valid ⟹ both outputs exist, are fresh (epoch e), mutually consistent (joint commitment), and canonical (root-pinned). q* is not part of I — say that explicitly, because half the bypasses target making q* load-bearing.

2. Attack enumeration grouped by target:
   - Group A: corrupt the inputs (B_P, B_H, m)
   - Group B: corrupt the arithmetic (rounding, units, degenerate values)
   - Group C: corrupt the join (TOCTOU, replay, partial forgery, fallback)
   - Group D: corrupt the assignment (chunk clustering, oscillation)
   - Group E: verkle/provenance-specific substitutions
   - Group F: side channels

For each: name, exact mechanism, deterministic mitigation with exact rule.

I'll aim for maybe 14–18 attacks, each tight. Use tables sparingly — actually a numbered list with bolded names and "Mechanism / Mitigation" lines might read better than a giant table. Given the density, a compact format: **A1 — name**: mechanism sentence(s); **Mitigation:** exact rule. Maybe group headers.

Also include the "meta-bypass": treating q* as security-relevant at all — the deterministic mitigation is architectural: strip q* from the trusted computing base; enforce soundness via commitments; q* only affects latency. And the fail-closed master rule.

Let me write out the exact formulas for mitigations:

- Clamping: q* ← min(max(q*, q_lo), q_hi) with q_lo = B_P,min/(B_P,min + B_H,max)... wait if q* is the P:H ratio then bounds differ. Let me fix semantics cleanly at the top: define q* as the fraction of total work W assigned to path P: w_P = q*·W, w_H = (1−q*)·W. Finish times: T_P = w_P/B_P, T_H = w_H/B_H. Setting equal: q*/B_P = (1−q*)/B_H → q*·B_H = (1−q*)B_P → q*(B_H+B_P) = B_P → q* = B_P/(B_P+B_H). Hmm, that gives q* = B_P/(B_P+B_H), not m·B_P/B_H. 

Alternative: q* defined as ratio w_P/w_H = B_P/B_H (from w_P/B_P = w_H/B_H). Then q* = B_P/B_H exactly, and m is a calibration multiplier (measured-vs-effective capacity correction, e.g., protocol overhead factor). So q* = m·B_P/B_H as the P:H work ratio. I'll go with: q* is the work ratio assigned P:H; m is a dimensionless calibration/overhead constant (e.g., accounting for per-message overhead differences between paths). That's faithful to the prompt's formula. Good — and note the sanity constraint: with m=1 and equal capacities, q*=1 (even split). Fine.

Then clamps: q* ∈ [q_lo, q_hi], e.g., [1/8, 8] or derived from attested bounds. Degenerate guards: B_P, B_H ≥ B_floor > 0.

Rebalancing rule (deterministic, estimate-free): chunked execution with chunk size c; maintain residuals r_P, r_H (remaining estimated time); assign each next chunk to argmin residual; tie → P. This is greedy list scheduling; makespan ≤ optimal + c; robust to any measurement error because it self-corrects every chunk. Keep q* only as initial hint. That's a strong deterministic mitigation for all of Group A/D measurement attacks: the attack then shifts at most one chunk.

Join commitment: C_e = H("join" ‖ epoch_e ‖ q*_fixedpoint ‖ root_P ‖ root_H) where root_P = verkle root of P's delivered witness set, root_H = header root. Gate compares C_e to expected C*_e pre-committed at epoch start (derived from the request). Any mismatch ⇒ reject. This kills TOCTOU (#4), substitution (#14 partially), replay (#5 via epoch), commit-then-diverge (#17).

Canonicality: root_H must equal the root pinned by the sync-committee-signed latest finalized header, with slot freshness slot_H ≥ current_slot − Δ. Kills #6.

Nullifiers: processed (epoch, requester) pairs inserted into verkle nullifier tree; inclusion proof required absent. Kills replay across forks since forks share the nullifier root lineage... careful: cross-fork replay — nullifier tree is part of state, so a fork lacking the nullifier would accept; mitigate by requiring H-root canonicality anyway (already #6). Good, layered.

Probe integrity: challenge-response throughput probe: verifier sends n chunks each containing fresh nonce n_i; responder returns MAC_k(n_i ‖ chunk_i) chained: n_{i+1} = H(n_i ‖ resp_i) so responses can't be precomputed or parallelized-ahead; measured B = (bytes acked)/(time to last ack), take min over j windows: B := min_j B_j. Spoofing upward requires actually processing at that rate. Downward spoofing (self-deflation) possible by a lazy peer — handled by bonding/slashing: peer posts bond, gate uses max(B_self_reported...) hmm, simpler: peer selection requires attested B ≥ B_need with slashing if window min falls below attested by >ε. Stake-weighted median for multi-reporter aggregation: sort reports by value, walk cumulative stake, take value at 50% cumulative stake. Require total reporting stake ≥ 2/3 of bonded set else fail-closed.
